News.title: My mafia boss dad taught me fallout of being a rat at 8 – but code of silence almost destroyed me, Mob Wives star says
News.content:
MOB Wives star Renee Graziano was just eight years old when she learned what it meant to be a rat.

Most children don’t grow up learning about the consequences of breaking the mafia’s code of silence.





Yet being the daughter of a high-ranking member of the Bonanno crime family was anything but ordinary.

Her father, Anthony Graziano, was a feared Bonanno captain who spent years in prison on racketeering, extortion, and tax-related convictions.

At home, however, he enforced one simple rule: don’t ask questions and don’t talk about what happens in the house.

Anthony didn’t speak to his daughters for several years following the release of the VH1 hit Mob Wives which first aired in April 2011 and ran for six seasons.



Renee said he felt that crucial code of honor had been broken.

Yet younger sister Jennifer, who produced the show, believed that films like Goodfellas and The Godfather often glamorized organized crime or centered exclusively on the men involved.

She wanted to tell a different story — one that exposed the harsh reality and lasting consequences for the women and children left behind, forced to rebuild their lives while those men served time in prison.

All members of mafia families were told that critical vow of silence — known as Omertà — and became one of the defining lessons of Renee’s childhood.



Those early learnings centered around a piggy bank stuffed with cash.

Renee, now 56, innocently told her father, who died aged 79 in 2019, that her older sister Lana had been taking money from it.

“He told me, ‘Don’t you ever tell on anybody,’” she said. “I learned to keep things to myself.

“My oldest sister used to have me wait in the hallway, and she would play chicky, like, in other words, looking for the cops.

“But there were no cops in our house. I was just looking for my father so she would turn it upside down. She would take the salad tongs, a flashlight, and she would pull out all the big bills.”



One day, dad Anthony decided to crack it open.

“But one day my father was like, all right, come on, Renee, let’s crack the piggy bank. He taught me how to count money,” she continued.

“He cracks it open and he puts me on first. He puts me on the table, gets the mallet, cracks it open, and there’s, uh, no big bills.

“And he says to me, Renee, where’s all the money? And I told him that Lana took it.

“‘Boom!’ he said, ‘don’t you ever tell anybody.’ And I was very confused because he asked me a question. But now he’s telling me to say nothing. So as an eight-year-old, all of this is running through my head.



“He said ‘I don’t care who asks you a question. You never say anything’. That was my first experience of what tattling was.”

While Renee knew him simply as Dad, Anthony Graziano was a powerful figure within the Bonanno crime family, one of New York City’s infamous Five Families.

Convicted on racketeering, extortion and tax-related charges, he spent a total of 22 years in prison spread across three different terms for racketeering, tax evasion and extortion, but remained a respected figure in organized crime.



Despite leaving school after seventh grade, Anthony built a formidable reputation as one of the family’s biggest earners, rising through the ranks from capo to consigliere under Bonanno boss Joseph “Big Joey” Massino.

The Bonanno family, alongside the Gambino, Genovese, Lucchese and Colombo families, formed the upper echelon of New York’s Mafia hierarchy.

Their influence stretched across illegal gambling, loansharking, labor racketeering and other criminal enterprises that generated millions of dollars over decades.

As a child, however, Renee knew little about any of that. Her father told her he ran a trucking company.

“I didn’t realize we were different until I heard other kids talk about their dads’ jobs,” she said.



“That’s when I started noticing things — the suits, the jewelry, the late nights. But you know what? I liked it.”

Still, her childhood felt normal.

“My father was the guy buying candy for all the kids, taking care of everyone. That’s what mattered to me,” she said.

“My father, to this day, is my hero. He was always there to solve every problem and grace us with a fur coat that fell off the back of the truck. He used to take me to work with him.

“He had a personality larger than life to match his heart.”



At 16, she got her first glimpse of how differently the outside world viewed him.

“I was at the end of the bar with a friend and this guy came over and he said he wanted to meet my dad because he was a captain,” she recalled.

“I remember being so taken aback and saying, ‘My father doesn’t drive a boat. My father doesn’t have a ship.’



“I went home and cried and then I asked him if he drove a boat. Was he driving cruise ships?

“I didn’t realize that I was different from all the other children until one day all the kids were chit-chatting and they were saying their fathers worked nine to five, and I was like, my dad works five to nine.

“Most kids learned about the birds and the bees at that age.I learned about captains and soldiers.”

Years later, Renee came to realize that the lesson her father taught her about secrecy had consequences far beyond organized crime.

Dating proved difficult. She said trying to find a boyfriend “sucked” – boys were either scared of her family or used her to get close to the mob.



“Guys were always running away from my father or running towards my father, so I had to make this decision for myself. What is it about me that I’m going to figure out that guys will stay for me?

“I think I became promiscuous because of that lifestyle, too. I couldn’t work out if a guy likes me, or does he like my father more?”

As a teenager, Renee said she also struggled with insecurity despite her father’s reputation.

“People think growing up like that makes you feel powerful,” she said. “For me, it didn’t.

“I think I was addicted to power, money, and men even before I was addicted to a substance.”



She claims she also experienced abuse in relationships at a young age. After one boyfriend hit her, she finally told her father.

“We drove to a restaurant. He told me not to look out the window,” she said.

“I didn’t hear what happened, but my ex showed up later with a cast.”

A stormy marriage to ex-con Hector Pagan gave Renee her beloved son AJ, but a lifetime of recrimination and anger.

With her father’s secrecy ideal sewn into her fabric, she kept everything in. It’s something she bitterly regrets.



“I tell this story lightheartedly,” she continued.

“However, it affected me tremendously throughout my whole entire life where I was constantly holding secrets that weren’t mine.

“I would keep secrets about my ex-husband when I shouldn’t have.”

Renee ultimately left the marriage and has said she turned to drink and drugs to ease her pain.

Pagan re-entered Renee’s life in 2011 while she was recovering from serious medical complications and fighting for survival in hospital.



“I had bad plastic surgery gone wrong and I was dying,” she recalled.

“I lost over six pints of blood and was in the hospital for months.

“That’s when he came back into my life. I believed him — but he only came back to entrap my father. He knew exactly who my father was. He used me. He was like everyone else. He just wanted to get closer to the action.”

Not long after Anthony was arrested again, and Renee began to suspect something was wrong.

“I knew something wasn’t right,” she said.



“But I never thought it was him [Pagan]. I found out like everyone else — through the media. When the world knew, I knew.”

Pagan had turned Graziano into the cops. Just three months after being released from a 12-year prison stretch, he was heading back inside.

After the truth emerged, Renee made a discovery she says still haunts her.

“When everything came out, I found his watch box. I thought I could sell them,” she said.

“But when I had them checked, I found out they were fake — and they all had wires in them. Mine included.



“You put a wire on my wrist that could have taken me away from my son. That’s the level someone will go to to save themselves.”

Pagan was released on parole early in 2024 after being sentenced to 11 years in jail for murder in 2014.

Together with two mob associates, Pagan targeted an auto body shop to heist tens of thousands of dollars from James Donovan, a check-casher associated with the Luchese crime family.

During the robbery, Pagan shot Donovan in the back, striking Donovan’s femoral artery, causing him to bleed to death.

Renee, meanwhile, is back in New York after a spell in the Florida sunshine and focused on moving forward.



She has conquered some addiction demons and is now involved in an immersive theater production called Married by the Mob.

There is also a body-care line, a memoir in the works alongside plans for future books.

There is also the small matter of Mob Wives returning for a sixth season.

Producers hope the show will return later this year, with Renee once again set to hit the big screen and take multiple trips down a memory lane overflowing with bad memories and experiences.

However her past, she claims, has made her stronger and more confident within herself.



“I’ve been celibate for nearly three years,” she said. “It was a choice based on self-respect.”

Despite everything she has endured, there are no regrets.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I try to laugh at what I’ve been through,” Renee said. “I’m smarter and wiser now. If I had the chance to live it all over again, I would. I would never change being my father’s daughter.”

News.title: Brits being plied with cheap booze, drugged & robbed in spiking ‘epidemic’ at ‘lion’s den’ clubs in tourist hotspot
News.content:
DENS OF SIN Brits being plied with cheap booze, drugged & robbed in spiking ‘epidemic’ at ‘lion’s den’ clubs in tourist hotspot

WITH a reputation for being a squeaky-clean, low-crime, dream holiday destination, more than 400,000 Brits flock to Japan every year.

But holidaymakers visiting Tokyo told The Sun that they were drugged by scammers in Kabukichō – a popular clubbing area known as the Japanese capital’s “sleepless town”.





Angelica Yanez, 36, travelled to Japan from California with her partner for was their first trip abroad together.

She told The Sun she was drugged in a Tokyo club before being made to pay thousands, while her boyfriend was forced to fork out almost £1,500 for just two drinks.

Antonio, whose name has been changed, said he had more than £650 charged to his card, and his friend lost more than £4,000.

Some suspect bars are involved in the racket, targeting foreigners. There are also rumours that the touts are linked to the Yakuza, one of the world’s deadliest gangs.

Both Antonio and Angelica claimed that cops did not take them seriously when they reported the crimes.

Angelica had spent nine days visiting Osaka, Kyoto, Hiroshima and Tokyo with her partner.

For their final night in the Japanese capital, the couple decided to go to a baseball game – which she says was ruined by scammers who targeted her in the street.

Angelica told The Sun: “They robbed us from having a great time in Japan to having the worst experience of our life. We want to say that was so much fun, but they took that away.”



They say they had been looking for a place to have a few drinks after the game when a man approached them and offered to take them to a good bar.

Angelica suspects he actually led them to a brothel, where she was separated from her partner, taken to a booth and offered drinks.

Scared and confused, she refused, but then she says the woman produced a small container and offered her a sniff.



“She said it was cocaine,” Angelica said. “I said ‘No, I’ve never had cocaine in my life. I don’t want that’.”

But she claimed that the woman “moved the container under her nose” and made her inhale.

Angelica told The Sun: “Five seconds after that, I passed out. I’ve never experienced anything like that. It was really scary.”

Luckily, Angelica’s partner came to find her and helped her escape.

But he had been presented with a huge bill and argued with the bar staff.



He eventually agreed to pay £1,500 for two drinks to get his girlfriend to safety.

Screaming in terror as she left the club, Angelica said: “People came up to me, and I just kept pushing everyone away. The next thing I know, I had the cop next to me holding my arm.”

Police took her to the station and claimed she had punched someone, the couple said.



Cops allegedly demanded a huge fine and Angelica refused, asking for a lawyer.

With the embassy closed, she says she was taken to a jewellery shop by her alleged victim, where she agreed to pay £1,500 for gold as “compensation” instead of the fine.

Angelica said police told her tests for cocaine came back clear, and they didn’t believe she had been drugged.

She flew back to the US and desperately tried to get justice, but she felt “helpless”.

She told The Sun: “I thought I was dead, like trying to pinch myself alive for a whole month. It took me a while to come back to reality.”



8 Credit: Getty

She got her money back because she used a credit card – but her partner had used his debit card in the bar and lost thousands of dollars.

After her ordeal, Angelica’s impression of Japan “being the safest place to travel” was shattered.

She now rarely drinks and is afraid to travel abroad.



In the same area, Antonio, a 37-year-old businessman from Chile, was returning to his hotel with a friend after a night out when he says they were approached by a tout.

He was staying a hundred metres from the club where they were partying – but he didn’t make it back that night.

Antonio told The Sun he was “a bit drunk but very clear” after four drinks.

And he thought he was safe in Japan – saying it felt like a “friendly New York“.

While walking to the hotel, Antonio was confronted by a line of touts and one persuaded him and his friend to follow him to a bar, promising cheap drinks.



He said: “We were ready to go to bed. It was a fun night but why did we need to extend it?”

When they entered the bar, he says there were no other tourists, just nine girls – who he believes were sex workers.

Antonio said: “It was obvious to me at this point that something was going on, but my friend persuaded me to stay for just one drink. I knew I was in the lion’s den.”

After one drink, he said everything “went blurry” and remembers nothing else.

Antonio woke up the next morning around 10am on a sofa at a nightclub while being shaken violently and asked for money.



Huge men towered over him and threatened to beat him if he didn’t pay a huge bill that was being waved at him, Antonio said.

Disorientated, he told them he couldn’t pay.

Antonio said: “I knew I was like in a very bad situation without any escape.”

A woman sitting next to Antonio – who he believes was part of the scam – told him to pay or the man would do “horrible things”.

After refusing to pay, he says he was was escorted to a cash machine, where he seized his moment to escape and “just started running”.



Later, his bank account revealed that more than £650 had been withdrawn overnight.

Antonio called his friend, who had woken up in a club he didn’t recognise, and discovered that his bank account had been drained of more than £4,000.

The scammers had seemingly made small payments at coffee shops and bars before charging higher amounts at clubs.

Antonio said other survivors of drink spiking in Japan told him this was a common tactic.

He said: “They take your card and they buy some coffee and tap in to the metro. I was not able to walk and I don’t remember walking out. But they probably took my card and they went to these places.”



Antonio believes scammers want to make it look like tourists have had an expensive night out, so they pay for coffee and the metro to claim they tried to help them get home.

He said: “The scam consists in making you pay a lot of money for things and that’s not a crime… so they won’t touch you. They won’t rob you.”

Despite the huge charges racked up on their credit cards, Antonio claimed Japanese police didn’t take them seriously when they went to file a report.

They were passed around police stations and who allegedly told him “we don’t see these cases” for hours.

Eventually, officers allegedly told Antonio that the incident wasn’t a crime.



Antonio wanted to prove he had been spiked, but cops reportedly told him that he would be arrested if drugs showed up in his system.

Antonio said: “They told us, ‘if it’s positive you will be in jail until we can clarify if you were trying to take the drug you or if you were forced to take it’. That could take months – so it was not an option.”

For several days after the incident, he experienced “a lot of headaches and physical pain”.

He eventually got his money back from his bank in Chile after reporting the charges as fraud – but his friend lost all his savings.

Antonio said: “I didn’t think that Japan was going to be a scary place… it’s very strange that this happens in such a futuristic country.”



He added: “Go to Japan anyway, it’s an amazing country – but be careful.”

The British embassy has warned that tourists are being tempted into dodgy bars by touts and then having drugs slipped into their drinks.

While they are knocked out, thousands of pounds are withdrawn from their accounts, or they are woken up and told they owe huge sums of money.

A spokesperson for Stamp Out Spiking said they received reports of Brits having their drinks drugged in Japan.

They told The Sun that cases reported to them have been men targeted “purely for robbery reasons, not sexual assault”.



The Foreign Office confirmed Brits have been targeted in the same area where Antonio and Angelica said they were drugged.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Brit victims were also approached by street touts known as “kyakuhiki”, the government warned, advising tourists not to follow kyakuhiki into bars.

Japan’s Foreign Office and the US Embassy in Japan have been contacted for comment.

News.title: Horrifying moment Spanish bullfighter is gored by raging beast as matador fights for life in hospital with 10in wound
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a matador is flung into the air and gored by a raging bull in Spain.

Tomás Angulo, 24, has been left fighting for his life after the horns of the beast ripped through his body and left him with 10-inch deep wounds.





Onlookers screamed in horror as they watched the bloody spectacle in Moralzarzal bullring in Madrid.

Harrowing footage shows the bull toss the fighter into the air with his horns before ploughing into the man as he lies bleeding on the floor.

His body is seen flying through the air like a rag doll before being savaged by the charging beast whose horns were smeared in blood.

Horrified matadors swarmed around the heaving mound of muscle and tried to distract him away from his prey.

Tomás collapsed helpless on the sand before another man pulled the bull away by his tail.

The 24-year-old had already been injured at the start of the fight on Saturday – but this second goring landed him in hospital.

The young man suffered three deep horn wounds on his left thigh with one wound hitting bone at 9.8 inches deep.

Another 7.9 inch wound severed through more than 2 inches of the femoral artery and a third tore 5.9 inches deep through several muscles.



Doctors say his condition is “very serious” after suffering extreme blood loss from the horror injuries.

The matador has also been slashed in the face and suffered multiple internal bleeds.

Tomás had been competing in the Copa Chenel, an international bullfighting contest.



In the qualifying rounds for the cup in May another matador suffered a sickening attack.

Horror footage shows the fighter being brutally gored in the groin as crowds scream in terror.

Albert Duran, 36, has been hospitalised in intensive care.

Dramatic footage captured the moment the bull reared its head upward and slammed its horns into Duran’s groin – launching him in the air.

Crowds recoiled in horror at ring in Valdemoro as the injured matador somehow staggered away from the charging animal.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Horrified onlookers were heard screaming as Duran was violently thrust upwards several times.

He was rushed to hospital, where surgeons performed emergency surgery on severe injuries to his testicles.

News.title: My best mate was murdered & left in UK river after night out – how jeans could be secret to finding killer 30yrs later
News.content:
COLD CASE RIDDLE My best mate was murdered & left in UK river after night out – how jeans could be secret to finding killer 30yrs later

JANET Murgatroyd, aged 20, was beaten, sexually assaulted and left to die on a river bank after a night out in 1996 – and her murderer is still at large.

Now, 30 years after her “brutal murder”, cops hope Janet’s missing jeans and knickers hold the key to finding her killer.





Janet’s best friend, Fiona Watson, and Janet’s mum, Mary, are calling for the killer to be brought to justice.

Fiona, who was with Janet as they drank in Preston’s pubs on that fateful night, said: “30 years later it’s still there, it’s still haunting you. And the impact it’s had on everyone’s lives.

“It’s still continuing to this day, there’s no peace to be got from not knowing what happened to her.

“This person is still out there, he’s living in the community. And that’s a worry. People should be worried about that.

“He’s living a life that she didn’t get to live, that her mother, her father, that I didn’t get to live. Because it changed me beyond belief and I never got that person that I was back.”

At only 20 years old “with her whole life in front of her”, Janet was studying at university and working part time at Lancashire Police HQ.



Late in the evening on Saturday 15 June 1996, she went to a pub with Fiona, and left with a young man she had been chatting to – heading for the city centre.

The pair parted ways, and Janet was seen on Penwortham Bridge which crosses the River Ribble between Preston and Penwortham, Lancashire.

Two witnesses, who were walking home from a night out heard a woman wail, and saw a man crouch down by the river bank.

On Sunday 16 June, Janet’s body was found in the River Ribble.

She lay unconscious for hours before being swept up by the tide, where she sadly drowned, it is believed.



Andrew Greenwood was convicted of Janet’s manslaughter, which was later quashed on appeal in 2004.

Now, Lancashire Police are renewing their appeal for people to come forward with information, focusing on the fact Janet’s jeans and knickers from that night have not been found.

A report came in from some children about clothing being found near the riverbank – but when police arrived, they had vanished.

Janet’s mum Mary, who is begging for the family’s decades-long search for answers to be over, said: “Janet Murgatroyd, my only child, was brutally murdered 30 years ago. The perpetrator is still at large; someone knows who this man is.



“Janet was on her way home after a day celebrating with her pal, having bought tickets for a holiday abroad. She couldn’t get a taxi, so she started to walk home to Penwortham.

“I need closure, this continues to affect me and my siblings. The killer needs putting away.”

Fiona added: “We were young, so we were enthusiastic about life, we were energetic. She was serious about her study and serious about working hard, wanted to achieve.

“Whilst we did go out, we didn’t go out all the time. She was just a regular 20-year-old young woman with her whole life in front of her and looking forward to it.”

Crimestoppers is offering a reward of up to £20,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction Janet’s murderer.



DCI Bryony Midgley of the Major Crime Review Team said: “It is 30 years since Janet was killed but we remain determined to get justice for Janet and her family.

“DNA technology and scientific approaches have significantly improved over the last 30 years, so I hope we will be able to take advantage of this as part of our investigation.

“We continue to appeal for information. It might be that you saw something that night or have information which you didn’t contact police about in 1996 or in the years since.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It might be that relationships and loyalties have changed since then, and you are now able to speak to us.

“Something you saw at the time might not have seemed relevant and you didn’t report it, but it could help our investigation.”

News.title: Ukraine blasts Putin-occupied Crimea with deadly drone onslaught as troops move to choke off Black Sea peninsula
News.content:
UKRAINE has blasted Russian-occupied Crimea with a deadly drone storm overnight as Volodymyr Zelensky’s troops move to choke off the Black Sea peninsula.

The Ukrainian President said he had blasted key targets on both sides of Russia’s £3billion Crimean Bridge in the early hours of Sunday morning.





A massive fire blazed at the Putin-occupied peninsula’s Kerch port, sending a 40-mile plume of black smoke into the air.

There, an oil and gas depot was attacked as Ukraine tries to cut Crimea off from Russian supplies.



Across the 21-mile Kerch Strait in Russia, the Kavkaz port was also ablaze.

One of the largest passenger ports in Russia, it is a hub for car and railway ferries and shipment of supplies to Crimea.

Petrol sales were paused in Crimea on Sunday after the targeted attacks hit fuel supplies.

Five people were killed and 28 wounded in the strikes, according to the region’s Russian-installed governor.



The strikes fuel rising speculation that Ukraine is preparing to launch its biggest attack yet on the Crimean Bridge itself, a key artery connecting Putin’s troops to the annexed territory.

Road and rail traffic slammed to a halt on the bridge as authorities shut it down for more than nine hours.



The peninsula was seized by Putin in 2014, eight years before Mad Vlad launched his full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Now Ukraine could be trying to grab its Black Sea outpost back from the deranged dictator.

Drones blitzed maritime logistics used to transport oil in the Krasnodar region and military logistics facilities this morning.

Zelensky said the attacks also took out critical Russian comms – four radar stations and two Pantsir systems.



Crimea’s ferry Panagia was attacked while bringing fuel to the the Russian-occupied region, which is suffering acute shortages after Ukrainian strikes.

All ferries across the Kerch Strait have been suspended after the attacks.

The Russian Defence Ministry said 239 Ukrainian drones had been shot down overnight.

Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on X: “Last night, our long-range sanctions targeted the occupiers’ military logistics, oil industry, and air defense.

“All of this is a just response to Russia’s brutal attacks against our people.”



He thanked his forces “for their successful work at a distance of about 300 kilometers from the frontline“, adding: “I am grateful to all our warriors for their precision and professionalism.”

Zelensky declared: “Russia understands only strength, and our long-range strength is certainly working for peace. Glory to Ukraine!”

Two people died and 14 were injured in Russian strikes on Poltava region in Ukraine overnight.

Dramatic footage also emerged of a fuel truck driver swerving to narrowly avoid a Ukrainian Hornet drone strike on the so-called Road of Death, which links Russia to occupied Crimea.

Video shows as the drone narrowly clears the truck’s roof.



Hundreds of trucks have been struck on this road through Ukraine’s Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia and Donetsk regions.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Crimean Bridge has been targeted three times by Ukraine since the start of the full-scale war, with major attacks in October 2022, July 2023 and June 2025.

The structure is weakened from repeated strikes but it remains open for light traffic.

News.title: Machete bikers & arsonists turning shops into ‘lava’… can UK’s first balaclava ban stamp out gangs terrorising our city?
News.content:
IT’S a historic city with two respected universities and proud links to the Robin Hood legend – but Nottingham is in the grip of a new menace.

The city looks set to become the first in the UK to ban the balaclava, to tackle gangs of lawless kids wearing concealing headgear who have taken over the streets, riding on ebikes, raiding stores and terrifying locals.





In recent months there have been two horrifying masked machete incidents played out in town in full view of families at popular precincts with the worrying side effect that it is now scaring people away.

On Sunday November 16, knife-wielding youths rode around on ebikes amid families and children who were visiting the city’s annual Winter Wonderland event. Panic-stricken Christmas market-goers screamed and ran in fear.

Daniel Drazewski, 23, has been charged with violent disorder and possessing a knife or bladed article in a public place.

And on January 28, at 7.30 in the evening, a teenage boy was attacked with a machete in a fight in the centre of Nottingham. Luckily his injuries were not life threatening.



Four 15-year-old boys, a 20-year-old man, a 16-year-old boy, and three girls – aged 14, 16 and 17 – have since been arrested on suspicion of affray and robbery.

Kids were also filmed breaking into and climbing on the top of the abandoned Debenhams building, which is a magnet for vandalism.



Four children, aged between 10 and 11, climbed the crumbling building in November, where they brazenly waved, dressed in black with their faces covered, to onlookers below.

Shopkeeper Kumar Singh, 29, who works at Imobile phone repair shop in the city showed us footage of two young kids wearing balaclavas, entering the store pretending to be holding a gun.

They slowly walked into the shop before turning and grabbing speakers on display and dashing out with them.



He said: “If I didn’t have this on video you wouldn’t believe it.

“I jumped over the counter to go after him but really I just wanted to scare them off. What can you do? What am I supposed to do if I get them, they’re kids?

“It is worse on a night after sundown. I work the evening shift from 7pm to 10pm and you don’t feel safe around that time. If you call the police they take a couple of hours to get here.

“It is children thinking they are invincible. If you’ve nothing to hide then there is no need to wear a face covering.

“If you’re committing crime then it’s a very nice shield. It happens on a regular basis. It is visibly children in early teens either very angry or violent.



“Not only that, these are often gangs of ten to 12 kids, with a couple on ebikes. Everybody on the high street gets this. They snatch mobile phones and hang around in Old Market Square.

“You would be shocked. They go into shops and steal. They go to Greggs, Holland and Barrett, Superdrug – they take whatever they can. They even steal from charity shops, nobody is safe.

“The high street is already struggling and then you’ve got this to keep customers away. Smaller shops will end up closing because they won’t be able to survive.”



Sandy Rubie, 50, runs her Caribbean takeaway van, Sandy Takeaway, in the middle of the town centre.

She said: “To be honest I’ve not had much trouble from the kids. I have been going for 36 years and many of them know me.

“They will come and ask for food and I have a rule that I won’t serve anybody with a facecovering on and they’ll take them off and say ‘alright, Auntie’.



“I do see that it is a problem in the centre and it means if they want to do anything naughty they can just cover their face. And it’s worse with ebikes because they can make a quick getaway.

“I’ve seen lately that the police are playing them at their own game and they have ebikes too so it’s not so easy for them anymore.

“It is a good idea to stop kids wearing balaclavas. They are very intimidating for some people, especially the elderly.”

Alan Arthur, 63, who was enjoying a pint of Guinness at the Old Dog and Patridge pub, said: “I’m all for them banning the balaclava. It should not be one rule for one and one for another.

“Anytime I have to go to a petrol station on my bike I have to remove my helmet to show that I’m not committing a crime – kids should be doing the same.



“Why are the authorities so slow to act? This has been going on for years now.”

The balaclava gangs feed into a wider problem with youth crime and antisocial behaviour in the area.

In St Anne’s, one of the most deprived areas of the city, a suspected arson attack on a corner shop in St Ann’s, Ranya Grocery Store, on June 6, has reduced the family business to a blackened carcass after a blaze broke out at around 4am.



While we were there workmen were repairing the telegraph pole after that caught alight and wiped out services for 50 homes in the area. A white mini parked outside is molten brown.

Residents nearby and in the flat above had to be evacuated with locals fearing for their lives as they spilled out onto the street to witness the flames licking up and engulfing the building.

Just as horrifying is the news that a young 13-year-old child has been charged with arson with intent to endanger life and arson with recklessness as to whether life was endangered.

The boy, who cannot be named for legal reasons, has also been charged with robbery and possession of a knife in public following a separate incident at a shop five miles away, taking place on the same day, when the shopkeeper was threatened with a blade and hundreds of pounds worth of items were stolen



He was also charged with one count of shop theft after items were stolen from a supermarket on May 9.

The boy appeared at Nottingham Magistrates’ Court on June 10 and will next appear at the same court on June 22.

Uninsured owner Abdul Assad, a 34-year-old father of three said: “This is devastating, very sad for the community, it is a family store and it does not make a lot of money. I have been running the store for four years and I do what I can for the community, letting them pay me later for food when they are struggling.

“This is my only source of income and now it has all gone.” Abdul doesn’t have insurance and he’s been quoted around £150,000 for the total repairs.



A Go Fund Me set up to help him has only raised £365 so far.

He said: “I came out in the night and it was so scary, everything was melting like lava. It leaves you scared because you don’t know if this is somebody targeting my shop, that they have something against me. I have got terrible thoughts running through my head.”

A neighbour, a father–of-three, who did not want to be named, said: “There’s been a spate of around seven or eight fires around here for the past six months with wheelie bins being set on fire and now it has come to this.

“It’s a real concern because you’re worried whether you could be a target and whether you are safe at your home in bed at night. We used to have a lot of problems with drugs down here and that’s calmed down.



“But it’s replaced with something far more sinister. I believe it’s always kids, who seem to have no fear of the repercussions of the damage they are causing.”

Another stark reminder of the level of violence in the area is a heartbreaking shrine located in an underpass which was the location of the fatal stabbing of much loved 20-year-old Marley Gascoine.

He was killed on November 10 last year, with a single stab wound, by 20-year-old Matthew Smith who then escaped on an ebike.

Smith was found guilty of manslaughter and will be sentenced in September.



Self-employed painter Kirk William, 47, said: “I think the main thing around here is that there’s nothing much to do. It’s a case of the devil finding work for idle hands.

”But I do think banning balaclavas could be a good thing, if you’re masking your face because you’re up to something then it’s a problem.”

To tackle problems in the city, Nottingham Council is bringing in a three-year Public Spaces Protection Order (PSPO) to crack down on certain nuisance behaviours, including busking and begging.

Council leader Neghat Khan said that concerns over face coverings have been raised and that the authority would run a consultation on the introduction of a ban, if opinion was strong enough.



She said: “It’s a serious concern, people on e-bikes – it’s 32 degrees and you’re wearing a balaclava. That’s not acceptable.

“There was a report published that said Nottingham was the seventh most unsafe place in the country. As the leader of the council, that’s not a tag I want.

“I don’t care who it is, any time, day or night, you should feel safe. This is your city and we’re not going to let criminals and others take it over.”

Khan added she would not “rest until we’re the safest city in the country”.



The council are encouraging residents, businesses and visitors to respond to the consultation before it closes on June 22.

Gold-toothed Dr Marcellus Baz, who grew up in a life of crime and deprivation, now runs award winning Switch Up, a youth organisation that diverts kids away from a life of crime through sport, education and employability.

His organisation and boxing gym is based in St Ann’s, an area known for its high crime rate which is 257 per thousand resident population, annually. The national average is 72 crimes per thousand.

The area is home to the troubled kids that are referred to his charitable organisation, which is backed by celebs such as Nottingham actress Vicky McClure and Olympic skaters Torvill and Dean.



Dr Baz said: “I support any proportionate measures that genuinely improve public safety but I wouldn’t want people to believe this is a silver bullet. It may form part of the response but it cannot be the whole response.

“Organisations like ours are supporting a balaclava ban as long as it is implemented as a wider strategy that looks at underlying issues to why young people are on the streets in the first place.

“I think this will help because when you look at offending behavior, it comes in three steps – intention, concealing yourself to know that you are not going to get caught and committing the offence.

“If we were to take the balaclavas away, you are taking away one of the steps, which makes it more difficult for people to commit offences.



“For me, the wider strategy needs to look at the underlying issues of why young people are actually out there in the first place.

“Why are we seeing young people involved in criminality and antisocial behaviour?

“But we must be honest that banning an item of clothing alone will not address these underlying issues”.

Mum-of-two Caroline Parsons, 35, said: “People say they are scared to go out at night but I am wary when I go out at any time, even during the day. I’m always on my guard and looking around me.



“You can’t avoid the kids on bikes with balaclavas because they hang around outside the One Stop shop, so you are seeing them all the time. You just put your head down and scurry on through and hope for the best.

“It really puts me on edge. It makes me wonder why they are hiding their faces.”

One mum, Amy Hodson-Ridgway, from Denton, Greater Manchester, welcomes Nottingham’s stance after she set up her own petition to ban balaclavas after her eight-year-old son, Ethan, was knocked over by a moped travelling at 45mph on December 20 last year, leaving him with serious injuries including a collapsed lung, head trauma and a broken tibia and fibula in his lower left leg.

Despite the clear footage caught on a Ring doorbell, police have been unable to identify the suspects due to the riders’ identities being hidden and the bike having no plates, leading to the case being closed just three weeks after the incident.



She said: “This single piece of clothing has turned our community into a breeding ground for lawlessness and fear.

“It’s a great idea for Nottingham to ban balaclavas altogether. I hope it happens and I hope other cities follow suit.

“Our lives have been turned upside down and all because kids were wearing balaclavas. I do not think they would have been riding like that if their faces weren’t covered.



“Ethan is now recovering but sadly the psychological harm is taking longer to heal. He now doesn’t want to play outside because we often see motorbikes driven by kids in balaclavas around here and it terrifies him.”

Her petition has over 60,000 signatures and can be found here.

A spokesperson from Nottingham City Council said: “Any proposal to introduce restrictions relating specifically to face coverings would require further consideration and a separate consultation before any decision could be made.

“We would therefore urge residents who have concerns about the use of face coverings in the city centre to make their views known through the current consultation.”

Matt Jarram, Senior Media and External Relations Manager at Nottinghamshire Police, said police in Nottingham are already seizing balaclavas from young people if they are involved in crime and anti-social behaviour as part of Operation Reclaim, which targets problem youths by addressing offending behavior and taking them home to their parents.



Any parents unable to control their children could face a fine.

Speaking about the operation, city commander, superintendent Chris Pearson said: “We will put measures in place which restrict their activity in the city centre.

“This can and will include taking away their balaclavas and making sure [they] cannot wear one in the city again.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The general public have had enough of [their] behaviour, and so have we. That is why Operation Reclaim is vitally important.

“It is a partnership approach to not only educate young people, support families, but also take strong action so that Nottingham city centre becomes a ‘no go’ area for behaviour like this.”

News.title: Agonising moment bungling DIY mechanic lets car roll down drive & smash through wall after leaving handbrake off
News.content:
THIS is the moment a DIY mechanic left the handbrake off – sending his car rolling down his drive and smashing through his neighbour’s garden wall.

Flynn Tasker-Davies was repairing the gearbox of his Suzuki Jimny when he made the embarassing blunder.





Video footage shows Flynn dropping the car down from the jack stand after completing the repairs.

But the 20-year-old had made one crucial error as he’d forgotten to reapply the handbrake – which had been left off while he fixed it.

Seconds after removing the stand, footage shows the car rolling backwards down the driveway, with Flynn sprinting after it in a desperate attempt to bring the car to a stop.

After realising he wouldn’t be able to stop the 4×4 vehicle – Flynn was left to watch in horror as the car crashed into his neighbour’s wall and motorhome on March 29.

Since sharing the video on TikTok, the clip has gone viral, racking up more than 227,000 views, with social media users joking ‘you can’t park there’.

The account manager, who “rarely” takes his car to the mechanics, says he now always ‘quadruple checks’ the handbrake is on when carrying out similar repairs.



Flynn, from Newport, South Wales, said: “I was trying to fix the car because something was wrong with the gear box.

“I had it up on the jack stand so all the wheels were in the air and the handbrake was off because I had to have the wheels spinning.

“I completely forgot that the handbrake was off, dropped it down and then it just rolled straight off the drive.

“It was such an easy, preventative thing that I just completely forgot about.

“It wouldn’t have happened at all if I’d put the handbrake back on before I lowered the car down.”



A stunned Flynn was left to watch in horror as the car rolled away from him and crashed into the neighbour’s wall – despite his desperate attempt to run after and stop it.

Flynn said: “I was like ‘oh my god, this can’t be happening’ – this is the sort of thing you see online; it doesn’t ever happen to yourself.

“It was a spur of the moment thing [to run after the car] – I thought I would have gained some super strength but it was but I shouldn’t have really ran after it, I could have been run over it.

“I was in fight or flight and I just ran after it. I stopped running and it was at that point I realised the car was done for.”

The car caused damage to his neighbour’s wall and motorhome, but Flynn says the cost of repairs were covered by the insurance company.



Flynn said: “They weren’t so much annoyed, it was more an inconvenience but they were glad that everyone was okay and there was no one hurt because it was only a bit of metal and brick that was damaged, no actual injuries or anything.

“It’s lucky there was no oncoming traffic or a pedestrian in the road.”

Despite having completed the gearbox repair seconds before the car rolled away, Flynn was never able to drive the vehicle again as it was written off by the insurance company.

Flynn said: “I’d managed to get the repair done but I didn’t drive it [the car] again.

“All the back door was smashed in on it – the car was written off in the end.



“I do kind of regret not taking the car to a garage for the repair but I wanted to sell it anyway.

“As much as it was an inconvenience, I got the insurance payment and got more than what I paid for it so it was the best of a bad outcome really.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “My warning to people would be don’t do what I did and make sure the handbrake is always on when you’re jacking up the car.”

Since sharing the video online the clip has gone viral, racking up more than 236,000 views, likes, shares and comments.

News.title: My girlfriend was labelled a ‘time-waster’ by the NHS while ‘staff watched football on TV’ – and then she died in agony
News.content:
LIBBY Instone lay in a hospital bed in agonising pain as her health rapidly deteriorated – with staff said to be preoccupied watching football on TV.

The 20-year-old university student was then sent home, having been repeatedly dismissed as a “time-waster”, but nine hours later she was dead. Now, her heartbroken boyfriend Theo Corbett, 23, has told The Sun how he helplessly watched his fun and bubbly girlfriend die without dignity.





Libby, from Billingham, Teesside, was repeatedly misdiagnosed with gastroenteritis in the hours before she passed away from infarction of her small intestine in the early hours of August 21 2023.

An inquest on June 1 this year concluded that neglect by the North Tees and Hartlepool NHS Foundation Trust significantly contributed to her death due to gross failure to provide basic medical attention.

The inquest heard the healthy student was treated as a “time-waster” – with her parents telling the hearing staff were preoccupied watching England’s Lionesses play Spain in the Women’s World Cup final on TV.

Theo told The Sun: “I think there was a lack of dignity in the way Libby was treated and then, frankly, in the way the family and the rest of us have been treated since, it’s just, it’s appalling, really.

“Had the things been in place that should have been on any of those occasions, there was a very good chance that what was wrong would have been spotted and that Libby would still be here.”

For days, Libby had been suffering severe abdominal pain, persistent lack of bowel movements and acute vomiting.

Accompanied by her parents, Susan and Ian, Libby attended the Urgent Care Centre at the University Hospital of North Tees three times within a 24-hour window but was continually dismissed, with staff failing to look for an alternative diagnosis.

Instead, the inquest heard she was reportedly treated by medics as an annoyance and a “time-waster” – and when she was finally admitted to a hospital ward, her family say there was a lack of basic care, resulting in her being sent home hours before she died suddenly.





Theo said: “It [the “time-waster” comment] sort of summed up the way she’d been treated, or it’s certainly the way it came across to us is that it was almost as if to get her in and out as quickly as possible.”

Her parents claim staff on the ward were pre-occupied watching the Women’s World Cup on the TV.

Mum Susan told the inquest: “All the staff were at the nurses’ station watching the Women’s World Cup final. All the nurses were stood around the telly.

“We asked if they could tell us where Libby was and someone said, ‘You won’t get any sense out of them until this has ended’.”

And later that evening, Libby was allowed to go home despite her constant pain and inability to keep food down.

In the early hours of the following morning, her bowel perforated, leading to a catastrophic collapse and cardiac arrest, and she passed away in her mum’s arms.

Boyfriend Theo described how he wheeled Libby to her parents’ car outside the hospital before she vomited a black substance.

He prayed she would simply go home and get better.



But at 2.30am the next morning, Susan called to tell Theo his girlfriend had died.

Just a few days before, Libby – who was studying Law at Newcastle University – had gone to London to visit Theo, also reading Law in the capital.

The pair excitedly discussed how they planned to live together while studying for the bar.

Theo told The Sun: “We were both just really looking forward to getting to that stage, and it really was just round the corner; we were going into our final year of uni and then after that, we were hoping to be able to move in together and complete those next steps.”

Libby arrived back home from the brief trip on August 15, with Theo set to head up a few days later.

But he said when they Facetimed the next day he “could see that straight away something wasn’t right”.

“She was writhing around on her bed, and she was complaining that her stomach really hurt,” he explained.

Her symptoms seemed to have come out of nowhere, and things got worse.



On August 18, Libby’s parents took her to the Urgent Care Centre, where she was prescribed anti-sickness meds and sent home without an examination, the inquest heard.

When Libby showed no signs of improving, including “constantly wretching and in a lot of pain”, they returned overnight, and she was diagnosed with gastroenteritis, given a saline drip and sent home at 1.30am.

By the following afternoon, she visited the UCC for a third time and was finally admitted to a hospital ward that evening, having waited six-and-a-half hours to be assessed.

The following day, August 20, Theo rushed up north from London and went straight to see his girlfriend.

He explained: “She was incredibly ill, and I could see that as soon as I’d gone in, just from the person that I’d known for the past couple of years…

“How someone could go from being so, sort of happy and healthy and fit, to being how she was on that day, it just didn’t make any sense.”

But again, Libby was eventually sent home, despite being “so weak and frail she wasn’t able to walk on her own”, and Theo said he had to find her a wheelchair just to get to the car.

He explained: “I wheeled her out to the front and put her in her parents’ car and gave her a hug, and hoped at that point that she’d be going home to hopefully get a bit better.



“But I knew how ill she was, and that was the last time that I saw her in person.”

Theo heard from Libby once more in a text at 7.30pm in which she said she was going to have a few more painkillers and then try t+o go to sleep.

He headed to bed at midnight only to be woken two and a half hours later with the call from Susan.

Theo said he felt powerless watching his girlfriend die.

“You feel completely helpless really when you’re seeing someone sort of deteriorate so quickly; you wonder what else you can do,” he said.

He went on to say: “Certainly for a lot of Libby’s treatment, it did appear there were biases.”

Of the inquest, which took place earlier this month, Theo said: “Families shouldn’t have to push and push just to find out how their loved ones died.”

He said there had been resistance from the trust throughout the “three-year fight”.

He continued: “It does feel like it’s sort of a vindication of what you’ve believed and what you’ve been fighting for so far.



“But, of course, no matter what ruling you get, it doesn’t bring her back.”

Theo said: “Libby was incredibly bubbly, funny, really bright.

“Her family and her friends all knew how bright she was, but I don’t think she ever sort of fully recognised how smart she was.

“She was just lovely, incredibly kind to everyone that she knew, and that’s one thing that really sort of has carried on after she’s died, people just remember how kind she was to them and how much of an impact she had on people’s lives.”

A spokesperson from North Tees and Hartlepool NHS Foundation Trust said: “We are deeply saddened by the death of Libby Instone, who was under our care.

“Our sincere condolences remain with her family, friends and loved ones during this difficult time. We accept the findings of the inquest today.

“We apologise to her family and continue to offer support to all involved.

“A thorough review of the circumstances surrounding this case has identified shortcomings in the care provided to Libby and her family.

“We are committed to learning from this tragic case and have implemented measures to strengthen the process to reduce the risk of similar incidents in the future.”

News.content:

Bedford train crash LIVE: Nine in critical condition after horror train crash killed driver and injured dozens

Bedford: Passengers on the tracks after high-speed trains collide

The King is "greatly saddened" by a train crash near Bedford that has left one driver dead and 89 people injured.

News.title: Mother, father and son jumped into crocodile pit to rescue toddler as new details emerge
News.content:
Mother, father and son jumped into crocodile pit to rescue toddler as new details emerge

The family who own Johnson’s of Old Hurst near Huntingdon have been described as "resilient" after they leapt into the crocodile enclosure to save a three-year-old boy

View 3 Images Tracey Johnson, with her husband Andrew, carrying one of the zoo’s crocodiles in 2009 (Image: Masons News Service / SWNS)

New details have emerged surrounding the rescue of a three-year-old boy who was thrown into a crocodile enclosure at a zoo this week

On Thursday, June 18 police officers were called to the Johnson’s of Old Hurst zoo near Huntingdon at 1.24pm by the ambulance service to reports that a three-year-old boy had suffered serious injuries. The boy, who sustained serious injuries while in the enclosure, was pulled out by staff from the zoo and received medical treatment at the scene before being taken to hospital.

The suspect, a 30-year-old Norfolk man who is not known to the youngster, was released on bail after Cambridgeshire Police officers deemed him "not fit for interview”.

View 3 Images (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

Man charged in connection with Edinburgh attacks that left five men injured READ MORE :

In a statement issued on Facebook, the zoo team announced that the Tropical House would remain shut out of respect to the victim's family, triggering an outpouring of support for Tracey and her staff from local residents.

The Sunday Times has now revealed that it was not just Tracey Johnson but her husband, Andrew, and one of the couple's sons, Edward, who jumped into the enclosure to save the child.

Andrew entered the enclosure soon after his wife along with Edward, 29, who is one of two siblings. Together they are understood to have prised the toddler away from the crocodile, before taking him out of the enclosure.

Chris Newman, director of the National Centre for Reptile Welfare, said he spoke to the Johnson family on Friday evening. "We mustn't underestimate how much of a difference Tracey made," he said. "She was first in there. She jumped in and dealt with an awful situation. She was then joined by her husband and son. It was a team effort."

View 3 Images Johnson’s of Old Hurst the crocodile farm in Cambridgeshire (Image: Newsquest/SWNS)

Newman added: "They are a resilient family but they are distraught. Their thoughts and concerns are for the child."

The newspaper also revealed the boy may have escaped death or further serious injury because the animal that bit him would have been fed a diet of offcuts of livestock, and might not have recognised the child as food.

The identity of the injured toddler has not been disclosed. Cambridgeshire Constabulary said in a statement: "A three-year-old boy from Cambridgeshire remains at Addenbrooke's hospital in a critical but stable condition following an incident at Johnsons of Old Hurst.

"The boy, who sustained serious injuries while in the [crocodile] enclosure, was pulled out by staff from the zoo and received medical treatment at the scene before being taken to hospital.

"A 30-year-old man from Norfolk, arrested on suspicion of attempted murder, has been released on bail while detectives from our major crime unit conduct further inquiries regarding this incident. The man, who is not known to the victim, was assessed as not being fit for interview."

Det Insp Verity McCann said: “Our enquiries are ongoing as we continue to understand the circumstances surrounding this distressing incident. Our thoughts remain with the boy, and his family and specialist officers continue to support them through this difficult time.”

Article continues below

The 30-year-old man has been bailed until September 18.

News.title: Tragic toddler dies aged 21 months after 'cow's milk diet' causes severe anaemia
News.content:
Tragic toddler dies aged 21 months after 'cow's milk diet' causes severe anaemia

Anaya Khaanan, aged 21 months, died from severe anaemia after being fed a predominantly cow's milk-based diet when she failed to eat enough solid food to provide necessary levels of iron

View Image Anaya Khaanan sadly died at the Royal Blackburn Hospital in Blackburn, Lancashire (Image: James Maloney/Lancs Live)

A toddler who was fed a predominantly cow's milk-based diet after struggling to eat enough solid food died from severe anaemia, an inquest has heard.

‌



Anaya Khaanan was 21 months old when she died at the Royal Blackburn Hospital on July 22 last year. The daughter of Mian Abdul Khaanan and Aneela Ikram, from Burnley, Lancashire, had developed anaemia after she had been "offered solid foods but was unable to consume sufficient oral intake to meet her iron needs".

‌



On the evening of July 21, Anaya's condition deteriorated and she was taken to hospital. Doctors decided she required a blood transfusion, but she died before it could be carried out.

‌



An inquest into Anaya's death was held at Preston Coroners' Court before Area Coroner Kate Bisset on Tuesday. It heard that Anaya had been born in Pakistan. The cause of death was recorded as severe anaemia caused by a milk-based diet, Lancashire Live reports.

The coroner returned a narrative conclusion and said: "Anaya Khaanan died on the 22nd July 2025 at the Royal Blackburn Hospital as a consequence of severe anaemia caused by a predominantly milk-based diet.

Article continues below

"Anaya was offered solid foods but was unable to consume sufficient oral intake to meet her iron needs, particularly when she became tired as her anaemia progressed.

"Anaya had been seen by the GP who ordered blood tests to take place and she was also seen at the urgent treatment centre on the 10th July 2025. At that time, a diagnosis was made of urinary tract infection and no blood tests were undertaken as they were not clinically indicated by her presentation on that date.

"Anaya became more unwell overnight between the 21st and 22nd July 2025 and was taken to hospital where plans was instigated for a blood transfusion to take place. Anaya deteriorated and died prior to the transfusion taking place."

News.title: Makerfield by-election result live: Cabinet minister refuses to rule out Keir Starmer departure after Andy Burnham win
News.content:
Labour's leadership battle is in sharp focus after Andy Burnham won the Makerfield by-election with 24,927 votes - giving him a majority of 9,231, while Reform's Robert Kenyon was a distant second

A senior Labour government figure today refused to rule out the resignation of embattled Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

Number 10 has insisted the PM will continue to fight on following Andy Burnham's emphatic victory in the Makerfield by-election.

But pressed on the issue of him quitting, Business Secretary Peter Kyle said this morning: “The reality right now is there are processes under way. There are people who seek to challenge Keir. I don’t know for fact what the next few days will entail.”

He said the PM was spending the weekend "making time to reflect on the political realities, challenges, and opportunities that he finds himself in." He further described the current situation as "a moment where there's clearly political uncertainty."

Reports today speculate the PM may set out a timetable to quit as early as Monday, despite his earlier insistence has said he "will stand" in a Labour leadership battle if one is triggered, with increasing pressure from top ministers and over 100 MPs to set out plans for his departure.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander previously urged him to set out a plan to leave office during a private conversation and yesterday Baroness Harman, Labour's former deputy leader said called for a speedy resolution, saying ministers could not be left “in a state of paralysis all through the summer”.

Andy Burnham convincingly won the Makerfield by-election - clearing a major obstacle on the path to No10. The 'King in the North' comfortably saw off controversial Reform candidate Rob Kenyon, winning nearly 55% of the vote.

Mr Burnham described the result as a "turning point" and said he had unfinished business in Westminster, nearly a decade after he left Parliament.

In the most consequential by-election in modern times, he picked up 24,937 votes compared to Mr Kenyon's 15,696. Rebecca Shepherd, of hard-right party Restore, came in third with 3,111. In his victory speech Mr Burnham said: “Everyone knows that politics isn’t working. Everyone can feel that the country isn’t where it should be. Tonight could, just could, be the turning point." As he left, he told reporters he was going for a pint.

Follow live updates below....

News.title: Met Office issues urgent 'water shock' warning after string of heatwave-related deaths
News.content:
Met Office issues urgent 'water shock' warning after string of heatwave-related deaths

The Met Office has warned people of the dangers of swimming in cold water as Britain braces for temperatures of up to 34C

View 3 Images The warning comes after 17 people died in open water incidents during a hot spell in May (Image: PA)

The Met Office has warned people of the dangers of swimming in the water - including cold water shock - as Britain braces for temperatures of up to 34C.

‌



Temperatures are expected to reach 32C in the south of England on Sunday and potentially 34C or higher on Monday, the forecaster said.

‌



As a heatwave grips the country, the Met Office urged people to be mindful that "sea-surface temperatures are not as high as they would be in mid-summer".

‌



During a hot spell in May, 19 people - most of them young - died in open-water incidents in areas including South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, Cornwall, Hampshire, Warwickshire, Cheshire, Pembrokeshire, Lincolnshire and Lancashire.

View 3 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Samantha Hughes, national water safety partner at the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI), said: "It’s important to remember that the water is still cold. Entering it unexpectedly can lead to cold water shock, causing a sudden increase in breathing and heart rate, which may trigger panic."

‌



She added: "If you find yourself struggling in the water, remember to Float to Live: tilt your head back so your ears are submerged, relax and control your breathing. You may need to gently use your hands to help you stay afloat, and it’s ok if your legs sink—everyone floats differently."

People should choose a lifeguarded beach where possible and swim between the red and yellow flags, Ms Hughes said. In a coastal emergency, people should call 999 and ask for the coastguard.

Water safety advice is available on the RNLI website and its updated app, which now includes a dedicated beach forecast, providing information on tide times, wave heights and sea surface temperatures.

‌



Aamber heat health alerts have been issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for the east, south-east and south-west of England from Monday morning until Wednesday evening.

A UKHSA yellow heat alert is also in place for Yorkshire and Humber, north-east and north-west England during the same period.

An amber extreme heat warning has also been issued by the Met Office for Monday and Tuesday for most of southern England, south-eastern and eastern Wales, and much of the Midlands.

‌



The alert flags potential health impacts for people vulnerable to extreme heat and heat-related issues for the wider population, as well as a potential increase in water safety incidents.

People in the alert area are advised to drink plenty of fluids and to keep out of the sun, and avoid exercising between 11am and 3pm, the Met Office said.

View 3 Images Temperatures could reach 34C on Tuesday (Image: James Manning/PA Wire)

‌



The UK's highest temperature on Saturday was 27.7C, recorded in Writtle, near Chelmsford in Essex.

Gregory Wolverson, deputy chief forecaster at the Met Office, said: "Some areas in the south and southeast of England are likely to see heatwave criteria met over the weekend, with the potential for temperatures to reach the low 30s in the warmest locations.

“Headline maximum temperatures for the period are: 32°C on Friday in East Anglia, 28°C on Saturday as the warmest air temporarily shifts away from the UK, 32°C in the south and southeast of England on Sunday and the potential for 34°C in the same areas on Monday as warm conditions build again from the south.

Article continues below

"There is a slight chance that hot conditions may persist deeper into next week, but confidence in this aspect is rather low at this stage."

He added that there is currently a 40 per cent chance of exceeding the current UK June maximum temperature record of 35.6C, set in 1957 and 1976. There is a lower chance of exceeding the June maximum temperature record for Wales.

Alongside the warmth, spells of rain are expected, some heavy in northern and western areas. Thunderstorms are also possible across central and southern England, while the south is likely to see a mix of cloud and brighter spells. Temperatures are expected to reach the high 20s quite widely.

News.title: Donald Trump hit with another blast from Georgia Meloni as Italian PM steps up photo row
News.content:
Donald Trump hit with another blast from Georgia Meloni as Italian PM steps up photo row

The furious row between US president Donald Trump and Italian PM Georgia Meloni has rumbled on after she told him to 'focus on his own popularity' amid tumbling approval ratings

View 3 Images Italian PM Georgia Meloni has told Trump to 'focus' on his own popularity (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Italian Prime Minister Georgia Meloni has fired back at Donald Trump after he insisted she asked him 'over and over' for a photograph at the recent G7 summit.

‌



The bizarre row began this week after the US president gave an interview with an Italian broadcaster claiming that Meloni "begged" for the photo during the meeting in France, a version of events Meloni branded "completely fabricated."

‌



Neither side has shown any sign of backing down in the days since, with the fallout leading to Italy’s foreign minister cancelling a planned trip to the United States.

‌



After a furious Trump posted on Truth Social that Meloni was "doing poorly in Italy" and had refused to let him use US bases in the country for the Iran war, she issued her own frosty response yesterday - hinting at his faltering popularity among American voters.

View 3 Images Meloni branded Trump's comments 'senseless' in the latest escalation in the feud (Image: giorgiameloni/Instagram)

Unquestionable proof Donald Trump is WRONG in reflecting pool row after 'vandals' claim READ MORE :

Trump blames 'vandals' for Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool damage as Olympian arrested READ MORE :

She wrote: "President Trump, these constant, unprovoked attacks are senseless. As for my popularity, being your friend certainly has not helped it, nor does it depend on my relationship with you. My popularity depends on my ability to defend Italy's national interest, and that is exactly what I have always done"

‌



"That is also what I did regarding the American military bases in Italy. Their use is governed by agreements that we have always respected, and that cannot be violated as long as I am Prime Minister. Italy remains a sovereign nation. In any case, my popularity is none of your concern. I suggest you focus on yours."

View 3 Images Trump and Meloni had enjoyed a close political partnership until the recent fall-out (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Trump's post had said: "Italian Prime Minister Gigiorgia [sic] Meloni asked, over and over, for a picture with me during the G-7 meeting in France. She is doing poorly in Italy with her level of popularity, possibly because she turned down the United States of America, a country that truly loves and protects Italy, when it came to denying Iran from obtaining or developing a Nuclear Weapon (But so did Nato, for that matter!).

‌



"She wouldn't even let us use Italy's landing strips or runways, a great logistical inconvenience, and this despite the fact the U.S. contributes hundreds of Billions of Dollars a year to protect Italy, and other 'so-called' Nato Allies. Now, after the United States defeated Iran militarily, she wants to be friends again in order to get her 'numbers up.' No thanks!!!"

He misspelled her first name in the initial post before later correcting it.

The furore marks the latest fracturing in relations between the two right-wing populist leaders, with Meloni having congratulated Trump upon his election victory in 2024 and the pair appearing to be strategic allies during the opening months of his second term.

Article continues below

Tensions began to show after he called her "beautiful" during a speech at the Gaza Peace Summit last year, with Meloni beginning to distance herself from Trump earlier this year over his military actions against Iran and his verbal attacks on Pope Leo.

News.title: UK high street giant on the brink of collapse as 150 stores at risk of closure
News.content:
UK high street giant on the brink of collapse as 150 stores at risk of closure

This high street mainstay has been struggling ever since a controversial rebrand some years ago

View 2 Images Around 150 TJ Jones stores are at risk of closure (Image: Donna Clifford/GrimsbyLive)

A major UK high street retailer could be forced to shut 150 of its stores if a rescue deal receives court approval.

‌



TG Jones, formerly known as WHSmith, has unveiled plans to close 150 branches across the country and stop paying rent on a further 120 stores as part of a three-year turnaround strategy aimed at pulling the business back from the brink.

‌



The retailer's rescue blueprint has drawn fierce criticism, with detractors arguing that closing outlets as part of the survival plan offers no assurance the company will still be trading in three years' time, as outlined in the proposal.

‌



Should a judge reject the plan next month, TG Jones could reportedly be pushed into administration, according to the Express.

View 2 Images The outlet formally known as WH Smith has been struggling since its rebrand (Image: Getty Images)

‌



If the plans are given the green light, TG Jones would shut 150 of its locations. A full list has yet to be disclosed, but creditors insist the proposal does not go far enough.

Speaking to Sky News, an anonymous creditor said: "It presupposes that the company will have sufficient cash in three years to pay an upside at all while the business will still have to repay its debts."

The same creditor also described the decision to pay 12% above base rate for the Modella-owned TG Jones name as "bizarre", adding: "It is bizarre that they agreed to pay millions of pounds for a completely unknown brand in the first place."

Article continues below

Meanwhile, an executive at one of TG Jones' landlords claimed it was unjust that Modella was "discounting profitable stores that on their own analysis are not overrented". The executive said: "Any landlord who keeps providing those stores is effectively giving a loan to the business of the amount by which the rent has been reduced - but not getting paid for it at anything like the same rates as Modella is getting."

A TGJones spokesperson responded: "We are aware of suggestions made by a small number of landlords in connection with the Restructuring Plan. We have engaged constructively with these landlords, as we have with other creditors across the estate.

"As a result of that engagement, we have improved the terms of the Plan to reflect feedback received. We believe these improvements demonstrate our commitment to achieving a satisfactory outcome for all stakeholders."

News.title: Italy Foreign Office warning as Brits could be fined 500 euros
News.content:
Italy Foreign Office warning as Brits could be fined 500 euros

The Foreign Office has issued travel advice warning UK holidaymakers

View Image Millions of Brits head to Italy each year (Image: Janoka82 via Getty Images)

British holidaymakers are being warned that they risk being slapped with a 500 euro fine when visiting one of the most sought-after destinations in Europe.

‌



Millions of Brits are set to head overseas during the summer months, desperate for some sun, a change of scenery, as well as a well-deserved rest. The Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the Government's foreign affairs department, plays a key role in keeping UK citizens informed when travelling abroad - offering travel guidance covering more than 220 countries and territories across the globe.

‌



In its travel advice for Italy, the FCDO cautions that "some Italian towns and cities have specific laws, and you could be fined for breaking them". This, the FCDO noted, can include activities such as eating and drinking near major churches, historic monuments and public buildings.

‌



It is also against the law to enter or bathe in public fountains across numerous towns and cities, including Florence and Rome, or to swim in the canals of Venice. The island of Capri is enormously popular with tourists and can be accessed by ferry from both Naples and Sorrento.

The stunning island nestled off Italy's Amalfi Coast is celebrated for its Mediterranean charm and rich ancient heritage. However, visitors are being made aware that bringing any disposable plastic items onto the island - such as bags, cutlery, plates, cups, food packaging, trays and straws - is strictly prohibited.

Article continues below

Should you be caught doing so, you could face a penalty of up to 500 euros. Additional FCDO guidance regarding Italy adds: "Illegal traders operate on the streets of all major Italian cities. It is illegal to buy items from unlicensed street traders. If you do, you could be stopped by the local police and fined.

"It's illegal to remove sand, shells or pebbles from coastal areas in Italy. You could face a large fine for doing so. It's also illegal to collect various species of flowers, plants and herbs from mountain and wooded areas. For more information, check with the regional authorities of the area you're visiting."
